title: The Robber and the Mother's Prayer

keywords: tale of the robber and the woman
full_text:
A hardened burglar in Baghdad scaled the wall of an isolated house at midnight, intending to steal gold and silver. Slipping through the courtyard, he entered a modest chamber where a single oil wick illuminated a bed.

Upon the bed lay a sick child, pale with fever, while beside the couch knelt a young mother, weeping as she prayed in the darkness:

'O Merciful Creator! You who nourish the birds in the winter storm, look upon my child! I have no medicine, no coin for the physician, and no bread in the larder; yet I trust in Your boundless compassion to deliver my little one.'

The burglar stood in the shadows, his hand resting upon his iron pry-bar. His heart was struck with an agonizing pang of conscience: 'Shall I rob a house where hunger and disease have already entered? Shall I be worse than the wolves of the wilderness?'

Tears welled in the robber’s eyes. He took off his heavy leather purse containing fifty silver dirhams—the fruit of his previous thefts—and placed it gently upon the table beside the medicine bottle.

He slipped out into the courtyard, leaving his purse behind, and climbed down into the street.

The next morning, the mother found the silver, bought medicine and nourishment, and her child was healed!

The burglar, transformed by the power of that midnight prayer, renounced crime forever, took service with an honest blacksmith, and dedicated his life to protecting the vulnerable, proving that conscience can awaken in the darkest hour.
moral: The sincere prayer of an innocent soul can melt the hardest heart and inspire genuine repentance.
